subject: Re: OrbitGlobe cutover — transient outbound failures (egress port entropy & MTU)
messages:
From: James Perez <james.perez@orbitglobe.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: netops@orbitglobe.com
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Outbound failures during cutover — intermittent 502s and retransmits

Hi Karthik,

We're in the middle of the OrbitGlobe cutover to the new Equinox NVAs and are seeing intermittent outbound failures from our on-prem services to a downstream vendor API. Symptoms: short bursts of 502/504 on our side, client retries, and duplicated SYNs in the capture. We've attached a short pcap with a reproducible test hitting the vendor API over the new path.

We kicked off a basic triage (checked firewall rules, routes look OK) but the failures align with peak concurrency during the traffic cutover. NetOps also saw a few kernel logs on the NVAs about ephemeral port reuse and an iptables log line that looks like port collision.

Can the Redwood team help triage? The cutover window is tight — if we can't stabilize outbound behavior we'll need to roll back.

Attachments: packet_capture_20260905_initial.pcap (pcap)

Thanks,
James Perez
Sr. NetOps Engineer
OrbitGlobe

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: James Perez <james.perez@orbitglobe.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound failures during cutover — intermittent 502s and retransmits

James — thanks for the heads up and the pcap. Looping in Marissa and Lauren from infra engineering and Connor from field ops so we can triage quickly.

Initial asks so we don't duplicate work:
- Can you confirm whether the NVAs are running DNAT+SNAT (full outbound SNAT) or whether you expect source-address preservation?
- Please share the Equinox NVA NAT config snippet and any sysctl changes applied during the cutover.
- If possible, a short tcpdump during a reproducer that includes the SYN/SYN-ACK sequence (we'll look for port reuse/TTL/DF flags/ICMP "frag needed").

From glancing at the pcap I see: repeated SYNs and a flurry of RSTs keyed to the same source ports, which could indicate either ephemeral port collisions under high concurrency or a middlebox rewriting ports in a way that confuses connection tracking. Also looking for MTU/fragmentation signs (ICMP unreachable type 3 code 4).

Immediate mitigation options we can discuss:
- Short-term: route high-risk egress traffic to a dedicated outbound pool while we triage (we have a dedicated-out-001 pool that avoids the new NVAs).
- Mid-term: increase ephemeral port entropy / change SNAT strategy and enforce MSS clamp on the path.

Marissa/Lauren/Connor — can you pick this up? James: we can schedule a 30-min war-room if you'd like.

—Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, James Perez <james.perez@orbitglobe.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2026 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound failures during cutover — quick triage & recommended changes

Thanks — I pulled the pcap and did a short correlation with the Equinox config you sent on Slack. Summary of findings so far:

1) Ephemeral port exhaustion / collision pattern
- During burst tests we see many flows using the same source port range. The Equinox NVAs are performing 1:1 SNAT for outbound but are allocating translated ports from a narrow ephemeral range configured on the NVA (default on the vendor image). Under concurrent egress, port reuse is happening in <1s windows which leads to connection tracking ambiguity and RSTs once the vendor API replies to a reused tuple.

2) MTU / fragmentation interaction
- I see multiple packets with DF set and "Fragmentation needed" ICMPs in the capture. The downstream path to the vendor is enforcing a lower path MTU and some flows are seeing dropped fragments. That also amplifies retry behavior and may cause partial handshake failures.

3) Middlebox rewrite edge cases
- The NVA is also reordering source/destination transiently during health-check failover; when it fails back the tuple can be rewritten causing a different translated port to appear at the vendor and confusing the originator's retransmit timeout logic.

Recommended immediate actions (we can do these in the cutover window):
- Temporary routing fallback: move OrbitGlobe egress for the vendor's CIDR to Redwood dedicated-out-001 (avoids the new NVAs) — we can flip this in a 15-min maintenance window.
- Increase NVA ephemeral port range: bump to at least 32k ephemeral ports and ensure port randomization enabled. Attach: nva-config-snippet.txt.
- Enforce MSS clamp on client-facing side (1440) to avoid DF/fragmentation issues across the vendor path.
- Short-term conntrack timeout tuning: reduce reuse aggression (increase TCP timeout for tracking established flows to avoid rapid recycling).

If fallback is acceptable we'll schedule the routing change immediately and continue with the config changes as a follow-up. If OrbitGlobe prefers to keep the NVAs in path, we need Equinox to push an image with expanded ephemeral pool and randomized allocation — that's a vendor change and will take longer.

Attachments: nva-config-snippet.txt, cutover-checklist.pdf

—Marissa
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: James Perez <james.perez@orbitglobe.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: netops@orbitglobe.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitGlobe cutover — tests after NVA tweak

Marissa / team,

Thanks — we applied the NVA tweak per your snippet (increased ephemeral pool and enabled port randomization) and added an MSS clamp at the client edge. We ran the same concurrency test and attached a follow-up pcap. The frequency of the failures dropped but we're still seeing sporadic connection resets during peak (roughly 1 in 2000 requests). The vendor side continues to see ambiguous tuples occasionally.

Given the tight SLAs for this service, we'd like to request the temporary routing fallback to dedicated-out-001 while Redwood continues root-cause work (particularly the middlebox rewrite behavior during NVA health transitions). Can you confirm the rollback plan and any expected customer-visible impact?

Attachment: packet_capture_20260905_followup.pcap (pcap)

—James

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: James Perez <james.perez@orbitglobe.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 6 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitGlobe cutover — routing fallback approved and next steps

James — approved. We'll execute the temporary fallback to dedicated-out-001 and open an internal incident with a 1-hour immediate mitigation window. Steps we'll take (timeline in Drive link):

1) 16:35 PDT — BGP announcement change to prefer dedicated-out-001 for vendor CIDRs (expected 1-2 min convergence).
2) 16:38 PDT — Run smoke tests (internal synthetic + OrbitGlobe test harness).
3) 16:45 PDT — Monitor for 30 minutes; if errors drop to <=0.01% we'll keep fallback in place while root cause continues.
4) Postmortem: engineering will capture targeted traces and we will require Equinox to produce an NVA image with expanded ephemeral allocation and deterministic health-failover behavior.

Connor/Lauren/Marissa — lead the execution. Connor, please coordinate the BGP change with Edge Ops and confirm when the announcement is live. Marissa, please capture per-flow conntrack snapshots before/after the flip for the postmortem. Lauren, I'll own external communication and coordinate the vendor ask.

James — we understand the SLA sensitivity. Expect minimal customer-visible impact from the BGP change; the fallback uses our dedicated egress pool and preserves policy. I've linked the cutover checklist and the incident page below; we'll follow up with a short postmortem within 48 hours.

Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/OG-7219-cutover | HS-54621 | JIRA-NETOPS-1329
